newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: TRI working with airline on infotech.
newsitem.headline: TRI working with airline on infotech.

text.p: Malaysian telecommunications company Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) said on Saturday it had begun to work with the national airline on developing multimedia applications.

"We are looking closely at how to best develop new applications for the multimedia. And we have started to work very closely with MAS (Malaysian Airline System Bhd)," TRI chairman Tajudin Ramli told Reuters in an interview after an analysts' briefing following the release of its 1996 earnings on Friday.
Tajuddin Ramli is also chairman of national carrier MAS.
TRI operates Malaysia's largest mobile cellular telephone network, and also provides fixed-line services.

"We have got a number of things we are doing together. Anything above the ground, the (multimedia) applications will be handled by us (TRI)," he added, referring to the company's involvement in U.S.-based ORBCOMM Global L.P. He gave no further details.

TRI is a 30 percent shareholder in Teleglobe Inc of Canada which is part of ORBCOMM. ORBCOMM makes and operates Low Earth Orbit satellites, used in telecommunications and data transfer in the multimedia industry.
"As soon as we move to the new airport that is when we will be very active."
MAS is due to shift its operations to the Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Sepang on the outskirts of the capital, in 1998 when it is completed.
